Examples: real-data applications

Source: vignettes/articles/examples.Rmd
examples.Rmd

Every example below applies the functions of multiCollglm to a data set that was used in the literature to illustrate collinearity in a GLM, and compares the result with what was published. They follow the same structure: context, data, diagnostic with multiCollglm, comparison with the literature. The code of each article is run when the website is built, so all outputs can be reproduced.

Index

Example Data Family and link What it shows
Lee cancer remission LeeCancer Binomial, logit Reproduces the values of Lesaffre and Marx (1993) for the condition indices of the design matrix (190.78) and of the MacKinnon-Puterman matrix (329.95), and the ML-collinearity diagnostic.
Nitrogen dioxide Nitrogen Gamma, inverse Why centering the weighted matrix makes it singular for the canonical Gamma link.
Coal-mine fractures Mine Poisson, log Reproduces the published eigenvalues of the information matrix (condition index 2093.32).
Body fat bodyfat (TH.data) Gamma, log IRLS weights identically 1: WS, MP and X coincide.
Plastic injection Plastic Poisson, log Widely cited values that cannot be reproduced; large effect of the weights.
Comparison with VisCollin the five above several colldiag() equals method = "X"; where the IRLS weights make them differ; factors, weights and plots.

All data sets at a glance

The largest condition index (square-root scale) of each model for the four definitions available through the method argument:

library(multiCollglm)

lee <- LeeCancer
lee$x6100 <- lee$x6 * 100

models <- list(
  "Lee cancer (binomial, logit)"  = glm(y ~ x1 + x4 + x6100, binomial(), lee),
  "Nitrogen (Gamma, inverse)"     = glm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4, Gamma("inverse"), Nitrogen),
  "Mine (Poisson, log)"           = glm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4, poisson(), Mine),
  "Plastic (Poisson, log)"        = glm(Y ~ X1 + X2 + X3 + X4, poisson(), Plastic)
)
if (requireNamespace("TH.data", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data("bodyfat", package = "TH.data")
  models[["Body fat (Gamma, log)"]] <- glm(
    DEXfat ~ age + waistcirc + hipcirc + elbowbreadth + kneebreadth +
      anthro3a + anthro3b + anthro3c + anthro4,
    family = Gamma("log"), data = bodyfat)
}

tab <- t(sapply(models, function(m)
  sapply(c(WS = "WS", MP = "MP", X = "X", RAW = "RAW"),
         function(k) condition_number(m, method = k)$condition_index)))
knitr::kable(tab, digits = 2)
WS MP X RAW
Lee cancer (binomial, logit) 315.14 329.95 190.78 10808.13
Nitrogen (Gamma, inverse) 77.98 75.91 67.71 8790.65
Mine (Poisson, log) 28.58 26.45 19.90 2093.32
Plastic (Poisson, log) 876.84 899.04 595.74 73561.62
Body fat (Gamma, log) 352.04 352.04 352.04 3410.63

These are the values of Table 1 of the manuscript on multicollinearity diagnosis in GLMs (with intercept). WS is the default of the package. X ignores the IRLS weights (it is what VisCollin::colldiag() computes), MP is the definition of MacKinnon and Puterman, and RAW is the information matrix without any transformation.
